    Vietnam Airlines  /  Bangladesh operation launch  /  2026

    Launching the route is the easy half. Getting the money out is the regulated half.

    Every taka Vietnam Airlines earns in Bangladesh is trapped until six authorities have signed. This briefing maps all of them, in the order they must be cleared, and shows exactly what surplus earnings means in arithmetic.

    BIDA CAAB NBR Bangladesh Bank AD Bank Flyport GSA
    Backed by
    RoleGeneral Sales Agent, Bangladesh
    ScopeEstablishment, remittance, the monthly cycle
    Presenter noteDo not open with the company. Open with the constraint. Every airline entering Bangladesh discovers the repatriation problem in month four, after the money has already piled up. The value of a GSA is that this deck exists before month one.

    Sky and aircraft: Vietnam Airlines own brand imagery, used for this briefing

    The whole brief, in three moves

    Six clearances, one bank account, one monthly file.

    Move 01

    Establishment is sequential, not parallel

    BIDA permission, CAAB operating permission, NBR tax exemption and the AD bank account each depend on the one before it. Attempting them out of order is the single most common reason a launch slips a quarter.

    Move 02

    Remittance is formula driven

    Bangladesh Bank does not negotiate surplus earnings. It is collections, less disbursements, less a mandatory ten percent refund provision. Everything else is evidence for that one line.

    Move 03

    The GSA carries the monthly cycle

    Approval is post facto, so the airline remits first and files afterwards. That inverts the risk. Flyport holds the dedicated account, builds the file, and answers the bank's queries before they reach Vietnam Airlines.

    The map  /  What a new foreign carrier is actually inspected on

    Eight domains. Each one holds evidence a bank or an inspector can ask for on any given day.

    This is the standing requirement set Flyport maintains for a newly appointed carrier. It is not a launch checklist that gets filed away. It is the permanent shape of the file.

    Domain 01

    Corporate and legal

    Trade licence, Tax Identification Certificate, Business Identification Certificate, and the corporate instruments that make the local presence real.

    Domain 02

    BIDA and expatriate

    Branch office permission, expert e-visa recommendation, work permit, and the one to five expatriate to local staffing ratio.

    Domain 03

    CAAB and aviation

    Flight operation permission, approved passenger fare and cargo tariff, filed schedule, and the GSA appointment with its No Objection Certificate.

    Domain 04

    NBR and tax

    Double taxation relief under the Bangladesh and Vietnam agreement, plus a live tax exemption certificate the AD bank can rely on.

    Domain 05

    Bangladesh Bank and FX

    Waiver of the outward remittance clauses, notification of the GSA appointment, monthly reporting, and monthly post facto approval.

    Domain 06

    AD bank and remittance

    A dedicated account and a segregated transaction record for the carrier, and the bank acting as the airline's filing agent to Bangladesh Bank.

    Domain 07

    Financial statements and controls

    Books that reconcile to the bank statement line by line, because the statement is the only document the regulator accepts without a copy of anything else.

    Domain 08

    GSA operations and manpower

    City office, airport office, cargo village space, ground handling and catering arrangements, and the people who staff them.

    Presenter noteColour is doing work here. Gold is establishment, teal is the money regulator, magenta is what Flyport carries. Point that out once, then let it run for the rest of the deck.
    The map  /  Structure

    A foreign carrier cannot simply open an office and sell its own tickets.

    What the branch office can and cannot do

    • BIDA branch and liaison office permission covers representing a foreign airline in Bangladesh. That is the legal basis for a local presence at all.
    • Airline general sales agency and freight agency activity sits in a locally reserved category, so the selling entity has to be Bangladeshi owned.
    • This is precisely why Vietnam Airlines is represented through Flyport Limited rather than a wholly foreign owned entity. The structure is not a preference, it is the compliant path.
    • The two entities are not interchangeable. The branch office holds the permission and the expatriate; the GSA holds the account, the sales, and the file.
    Consequence for the money

    Collections land in a Flyport held account, in the airline's name and for the airline's benefit

    Under SPA Circular No. 02 of 21 November 2021, a resident general sales agent acting for more than one carrier must maintain a separate bank account for each of them, so that collections from each operation are never commingled.

    Vietnam Airlines therefore gets a ring fenced account from day one, and a bank statement that can be handed to Bangladesh Bank without redaction or explanation. That is what makes the monthly file provable.

    Presenter noteThis is the slide that converts the GSA from a commercial choice into a regulatory necessity. Say the sentence about the reserved category slowly.
    The map  /  Sequence

    Three phases. Nothing in phase two starts before phase one closes.

    Phase 1  .  Standing up

    Legal presence and traffic rights

    • Designation under the Bangladesh and Vietnam Air Services Agreement
    • BIDA branch office permission through the One Stop Service portal
    • Trade licence, TIN and BIN registration
    • CAAB flight operation permission and schedule approval
    • GSA appointment and the CAAB No Objection Certificate for it
    Phase 2  .  Financial plumbing

    The channel the money will use

    • USD 50,000 inward remittance and its encashment certificate
    • Dedicated AD bank account opened in the carrier's name
    • Waiver of the two outward remittance clauses in the BIDA permission
    • Notification to Bangladesh Bank of the GSA appointment
    • NBR tax exemption certificate under the double taxation agreement
    Phase 3  .  Running

    The cycle that repeats every month

    • BSP and CASS settlement into the dedicated account
    • Monthly collection, disbursement and provision computation
    • Remittance through the AD bank
    • Post facto approval file lodged with Bangladesh Bank
    • Annual renewals tracked as standing dates
    Where the calendar actually goes
    Weeks 0 to 4

    Designation and application set

    Designation, corporate documents attested through the Bangladesh Mission or home chamber, OSS submission lodged.

    Weeks 4 to 12

    Inter ministerial review

    Decided at scheduled committee sittings. Branch and liaison registration typically runs six to twelve weeks from filing.

    Weeks 8 to 14

    CAAB permissions in parallel

    Operating permission, tariffs and schedule advance alongside the BIDA file. Neither authority waits on the other.

    Weeks 12 to 18

    Banking and tax

    Account opening, waiver clauses, GSA notification, tax exemption certificate. Where a launch quietly loses a month if the sequence was wrong.

    Month 1 of service

    First remittance cycle

    First settlement, first surplus computation, first post facto approval. From here the cycle is monthly and unchanging.

    Timelines are Flyport planning assumptions from comparable carrier entries, not regulatory commitments. No authority guarantees a date.

    Presenter noteThe honest line here is that phases one and three are predictable and phase two is where launches slip. Say that out loud, it buys credibility for everything after it.
    01  .  BIDA  /  Registering local representation

    The permission letter, and the two clauses inside it that decide whether money can leave.

    The permission set

    • Branch office permission from BIDA, applied for through the One Stop Service portal and decided by an inter ministerial committee.
    • Expert e-visa recommendation letter, the document that lets the nominated expatriate enter on the right category.
    • Expert work permit, issued after arrival, renewable and inspected.
    • Waiver of Clause 7 and Clause 8, the two conditions in the standard permission that restrict outward remittance from the office.
    • Encashment certificate evidencing inward remittance of a minimum of USD 50,000 as initial establishment cost.
    Read this one carefully

    The waiver is not a formality

    Clause numbering follows the standard BIDA permission template. Confirm the exact clause numbers and wording against the permission letter as issued, because the AD bank will read the letter, not the template. Without both waivers on file, the bank has no basis to pass an outward remittance no matter how clean the monthly file is.

    1 : 5
    Expatriate to local ratio
    BIDA staffing compliance. One expatriate employee is expected to be supported by at least five Bangladeshi employees.
    $50k
    Minimum inward remittance
    Initial establishment cost for a branch, liaison or representative office, evidenced by an encashment certificate.
    6 to 12
    Weeks, filing to permission
    Planning assumption for branch and liaison registration. Committee sittings are the pacing item.

    02  .  CAAB  /  Operating permissions

    Traffic rights get the aircraft in. Tariff approval is what lets you sell the seat.

    Permission

    Flight operation permission

    Granted by the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh on the strength of designation under the Bangladesh and Vietnam Air Services Agreement.

    Permission

    Approved passenger fare and tariff

    Passenger fares are filed and approved. Selling outside an approved tariff is a compliance exposure, not a commercial choice.

    Permission

    Approved cargo rate and tariff

    Cargo rates require approval before space can be sold. This is the item most often left until after the first cargo booking has already been taken.

    Permission

    Flight schedule

    The timetable is approved in writing. Schedule changes need advance notice rather than retrospective filing.

    Permission

    GSA appointment

    The appointment of Flyport as General Sales Agent is filed, and a No Objection Certificate favouring the GSA is issued by CAAB.

    Ongoing

    Monthly traffic reporting

    Traffic, cargo and mail statistics are reported on a monthly cycle. This is a permanent obligation, not a launch task.

    Also on the annual file
    • City office and airport office lease agreements
    • Airport cargo village lease agreement
    • Agreements with CAAB and Biman Bangladesh for fuel uplift, catering and ground handling
    • A separate competency certificate if dangerous goods are to be carried
    Why this sits in a finance briefing

    Every one of these documents is also a remittance document

    The lease agreements, the ground handling agreement and the GSA No Objection Certificate all reappear in the annual documentation set that supports outward remittance. An operations document that lapses does not only create an operations problem. It stops the money.

    Presenter noteLand the closing card. It is the reason a finance team should care about a cargo village lease.
    03  .  NBR  /  Double taxation relief

    Treaty relief only exists once it is a certificate the bank can hold.

    The instrument

    Bangladesh and Vietnam double taxation agreement

    The agreement between Bangladesh and Vietnam for the avoidance of double taxation is the basis for the exemption. Bangladesh domestic law is now the Income Tax Act 2023, which succeeded the Income Tax Ordinance 1984, and the treaty continues to operate alongside it.

    Under the shipping and air transport article, profits from operating aircraft in international traffic are taxable in the enterprise's home state. In practice this means Vietnam Airlines' core international carriage income is not taxed a second time in Bangladesh.

    • Obtain or renew a Tax Residency Certificate from the Vietnamese tax authority for the relevant fiscal year.
    • File it with NBR together with a declaration of no permanent establishment in Bangladesh.
    • NBR issues the exemption or reduced withholding certificate.
    • The AD bank requires a valid, unexpired certificate on file before applying treaty terms to any outward remittance.
    The failure mode

    An expired certificate stops a clean remittance

    The certificate is renewed on an annual cycle. If it lapses mid year, the bank has to apply full domestic withholding to a remittance that is treaty exempt, and recovering that afterwards is slow. Flyport tracks the expiry as a standing calendar date rather than an inbox reminder.

    Also on the tax file
    • Valid tax exemption certificate from the National Board of Revenue
    • Updated VAT registration, trade licence and tax certificate
    • Advance income tax and refund statements, monthly
    • Challans for VAT and tax actually paid, monthly
    • Payment summaries for embarkation fee, airport charges and passenger development fee

    Treaty article numbering and rates should be confirmed against the operative text of the Bangladesh and Vietnam agreement before it is relied on in a filing. This page states the mechanism, not the assessment.

    Presenter noteResist quoting a withholding percentage from memory in the room. State the mechanism, promise the article reference in writing.
    04  .  Bangladesh Bank  /  The legal spine

    Four circulars from the Foreign Exchange Operation Department. Between them, they are the entire remittance regime.

    All four sit on top of Chapter 10 of the Guidelines for Foreign Exchange Transactions 2018. Read them in issue order and the current process explains itself.

    CircularDateWhat it changedWhat it means for Vietnam Airlines
    SPA No. 013 Sep 2020 Surplus earnings may be calculated on passage and freight collections, on actual realisation. Form P and Form P-2 abolished. IATA members file system generated BSP documents instead of passenger statements. This is the governing formula. It is also the circular that made the process workable, by removing per passenger documentation.
    SPA No. 0115 Nov 2021 ADs designated for outward remittance may issue drafts in foreign exchange favouring state owned fuel and oil selling companies, with the equivalent taka shown in the disbursement statement. Fuel uplift can be settled in foreign exchange through the designated AD, and appears as an evidenced line in the monthly disbursement statement.
    SPA No. 0221 Nov 2021 Resident general sales agents acting for more than one carrier must maintain separate bank accounts for each airline, so that collections from each operation stay separate. Vietnam Airlines gets a dedicated, ring fenced account. This is a legal requirement on the GSA, not a service promise.
    SPA No. 039 Aug 2023 Freight certificates move online. Form FF Export Prepaid is generated through the Online Export Monitoring System and Form FF Import Collect through the Online Import Monitoring System, replacing manual certificates. Cargo freight collected in taka has to be supported by a system generated Form FF collected from the exporter or importer before it can be remitted.
    Underneath all four

    GFET 2018, Chapter 10

    Paragraphs 1 and 2(A) of Chapter 10 and the relevant paragraphs of Chapter 12 remain the base text. The circulars amend and simplify, they do not replace.

    Issued under

    Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947

    These are directions to Authorized Dealers. The airline's counterparty for compliance is its AD bank, and the bank's counterparty is Bangladesh Bank.

    Standing check

    Confirm nothing has superseded these

    The Foreign Exchange Operation Department issues circulars continuously. Before each annual review, Flyport re-checks the FE circular index rather than assuming this set is still current.

    Presenter noteThis table is the credibility slide. It is also the one to leave with them. Note that the two circulars both numbered 01 are from different years; the numbering resets annually and it confuses people.
    04  .  Bangladesh Bank  /  The definition

    Three conditions, and remittance out of funds actually held.

    SPA Circular No. 01 of 3 September 2020 permits ADs to remit surplus earnings against passage and freight based on actual realisation, provided three conditions are met.

    Condition i

    All collections supported by bank statements

    The bank statement is the primary evidence. Not the sales report, not the ledger. Collections that did not land in the account did not happen.

    Condition ii

    Minimum ten percent provision maintained

    A minimum provision of ten percent on collections is held against refunds for unavailed journeys. The unused portion may be added back in a following period.

    Condition iii

    All disbursements adjusted

    Disbursements, accrued expenses, refunds, and income tax paid or payable are all deducted before anything is treated as surplus.

    The sentence that catches people

    Remittance is allowed out of the fund available, without borrowed funds, in the designated bank account.

    An airline cannot fund a remittance from a facility, an intercompany advance, or next month's collections. If the money is not sitting in the designated account, it does not go. This is why the account structure in SPA Circular No. 02 matters so much, and why a shared agency account is not an option.

    What replaced the old paperwork
    • Form P and Form P-2 from outgoing passengers are no longer required against ticket sales in local currency.
    • IATA member airlines file the BSP airline billing summary and the BSP statement summary, including system generated counter sales and excess baggage reports, plus a revenue and expenditure summary in the prescribed annexure.
    • Copies of supporting documents are no longer submitted, except bank statements and documents for taxes such as FATT, excise duty, embarkation fee and TDS.
    • Those documents are retained by the airline for production to the AD bank and to a Bangladesh Bank inspection team on request.
    Presenter noteThe retention point is the quiet one. The documents are not gone, they moved from submission to custody. If nobody owns custody, an inspection finds nothing.

    05  .  SPA Circular No. 02, 21 November 2021

    Separate accounts are the law, and the reason the file is provable.

    What the circular decided

    There are no restrictions on a resident entity acting as general sales agent for more than one airline. To bring discipline into remittances of surplus earnings out of respective collections, resident general sales agents must maintain separate bank accounts for each airline, to deposit collections from the respective operations.

    ADs were directed to guide multi carrier agents into that structure within three months of issuance, so it is long settled practice rather than a new requirement.

    • Vietnam Airlines collections never sit in a pooled agency account.
    • The bank statement for that account is, by itself, the evidence for condition (i) of the surplus earnings test.
    • Disbursements for the carrier are made from the same account, so the statement reconciles both sides of the calculation.
    • An inspection team can trace a single month end to end without a reconciliation schedule.
    The AD bank's role

    A dedicated account and a segregated transaction record

    Under the applicable foreign exchange guidelines the Authorized Dealer bank maintains a dedicated bank account and transaction record for each airline, to ensure proper segregation, monitoring, disbursement, reconciliation and remittance of airline related funds.

    The AD bank then carries out the procedure on the airline's behalf and submits the remittance documents to Bangladesh Bank. In practice the bank is the airline's filing agent, and the quality of the file it receives determines how fast it moves.

    Practical consequence

    Keep one AD relationship

    Holding the foreign currency account and every remittance with a single AD bank keeps one continuous transaction history for monitoring purposes. Splitting the relationship across banks doubles the explaining and halves the speed.

    Presenter noteThis is the slide where Flyport's structural advantage is a regulatory fact rather than a claim. Do not oversell it, just read the circular.
    06  .  The two special cases

    Fuel settles in foreign exchange. Cargo freight now needs a system generated form.

    SPA Circular No. 01  .  15 November 2021

    Purchase of fuel and oil in foreign exchange

    Airlines are permitted to pay local expenses from local earnings under GFET. To facilitate fuel purchase, ADs designated for outward remittance may issue drafts in foreign exchange favouring state owned fuel and oil selling companies.

    • The equivalent taka must be shown in the disbursement statement, supported by documentary evidence.
    • Payments by foreign exchange draft are reported in the online TM Form monitoring system.
    • The receiving oil company may encash, or retain the amount in a margin or approved foreign currency account for settling import payments.

    For Vietnam Airlines this means fuel uplift is a settled, evidenced disbursement line rather than an FX exposure to manage separately.

    SPA Circular No. 03  .  9 August 2023

    Form FF, generated online rather than issued by hand

    ADs no longer issue freight certificates manually. They generate them in Bangladesh Bank's own systems.

    • Form FF Export Prepaid is generated in the Online Export Monitoring System, in favour of the exporter.
    • Form FF Import Collect is generated in the Online Import Monitoring System, in favour of the importer.
    • The exporter or importer provides the form to the airline as support for freight charges received in local currency.
    • The airline collects it and submits it to the designated AD when remitting freight charges or surplus earnings to head office.

    The operational point: the form originates with the shipper's bank, not with the airline. Cargo sales made without chasing the Form FF create a remittance blockage months later.

    Process design consequence

    Form FF collection has to be part of the cargo booking workflow, not the month end close

    By the time a month end file is being assembled, the shipper has moved on. Flyport's cargo desk treats the Form FF as a condition of releasing the airway bill documentation, which is the only point in the chain where the counterparty still has a reason to respond.

    Presenter noteThe last card is the operational insight in this deck that a competitor GSA will not have thought through. Spend a beat on it.
    07  .  The monthly remittance process

    Five steps forward, one loop back. The loop is where months are lost.

    01

    Files received from the airline

    Passenger, cargo and disbursement files handed to the GSA and on to the AD bank.

    02

    Bank scrutiny

    The AD bank scrutinises the files and notifies discrepancies, or refers them back.

    03

    Surplus earnings confirmation

    The computation is agreed and the remittable figure is confirmed.

    04

    Remittance execution

    The AD bank converts and transfers to Vietnam Airlines head office.

    05

    Post facto approval filing

    The file is lodged with Bangladesh Bank for post facto approval, after the money has moved.

    The loop

    Discrepancy rectification by the client

    Step two returns to step one every time a file does not reconcile. There is no partial pass. A single unsupported collection line sends the whole month back, and the month behind it starts stacking up. Foreign carrier repatriation backlogs in this market are built almost entirely out of this loop, not out of policy.

    What Flyport does about it: the file is built to bank specification before it is submitted, and the discrepancy conversation happens inside Flyport rather than between the bank and Hanoi.

    The unusual part

    Approval comes after the money leaves

    Post facto approval is obtained from Bangladesh Bank after the remittance, not before it. Bangladesh Bank allows airlines to repatriate for up to six months of post facto approval, meaning funds can be remitted up to six months from the date of the documents last approved.

    The end to end flow is manual, with hard copy documentation submitted and verified at several levels. Nothing about it is automated, which is why the discipline sits in the preparation.

    Presenter noteEmphasise the inversion. Post facto approval means the airline is exposed between remittance and approval, and a rejected file after the fact is a much worse conversation than a delayed one.
    07  .  What is actually in the monthly submission

    Three core files, two supplementary. Everything else is evidence for them.

    Core file 01

    Passenger collection file

    BSP settled sales, direct and GSA sales, counter sales and excess baggage. The base for both the collection total and the refund provision.

    Core file 02

    Cargo collection file

    CASS settled sales and direct or GSA cargo sales, supported where required by Form FF from the exporter or importer.

    Core file 03

    Disbursement file

    Every local payment made from the account, including fuel, ground handling, catering, station costs, taxes and fees.

    Supplementary

    Miscellaneous file

    Excess baggage, postal earnings, extra charges and other receipts that belong in the collection total but not in the BSP report.

    Supplementary

    Refund statement file

    Refunds actually made in the period, which drive the add back of unused provision from the prior period.

    The binding evidence

    Bank statement

    The one document that cannot be substituted. Every collection and every disbursement in the three core files must appear on it.

    08  .  Documents required annually

    Eight documents that have to be valid on the day the bank looks.

    None of these are hard to obtain. All of them are easy to let expire. Each one, expired, stops a remittance that is otherwise perfectly computed.

    • Valid BIDA branch office permission, with the subsequent waiver approval in place.
    • Valid General Sales Agent agreement between Vietnam Airlines and Flyport.
    • City office and airport office lease agreements, plus the airport cargo village lease.
    • Agreements with CAAB and Biman Bangladesh for fuel uplift, catering and ground handling.
    • No Objection Certificate from CAAB favouring the General Sales Agent.
    • Valid tax exemption certificate from the National Board of Revenue.
    • Valid work permit for each expatriate employee.
    • Updated VAT registration, trade licence and tax certificate.
    How Flyport holds this

    One expiry register, reviewed monthly, not annually

    Each of the eight carries an expiry date and a renewal lead time. They are reviewed in the same monthly cycle as the remittance file, so a renewal is started ninety days out rather than discovered on a rejection notice.

    The compounding risk

    An expiry found late costs more than one month

    Because approval is post facto and the window runs from the date of documents last approved, a lapse does not just delay one remittance. It interrupts the chain the six month window is measured against, and the next file inherits the problem.

    Presenter noteThe compounding point is the argument for a GSA that runs a register. Make it, then stop talking.

    Eleven items, every month, for as long as the route operates.

    Annexure A, the shape of it
    SectionBroken down as
    Cargo salesSales through CASS, first fortnight and second fortnight, then direct and GSA sales, to a total cargo revenue line

    Presenter noteThe fortnightly observation is worth stating plainly. It is the most common source of a step two referral.
    09  .  The operating rhythm

    What a compliant month actually looks like.

    This is the cycle Flyport runs on behalf of the carrier. It is deliberately front loaded, so that a discrepancy is found while there is still time to fix it inside the same month.

    Week 1
    • Prior month bank statement drawn for the dedicated account
    • First fortnight BSP and CASS positions reconciled
    • Cargo desk closes outstanding Form FF collection for the prior month
    • Disbursement file assembled with challans attached
    Week 2
    • Second fortnight settlement reconciled and Annexure A built
    • Refund statement prepared and prior period provision movement computed
    • Surplus earnings computation drafted
    • Annual document expiry register reviewed
    Week 3
    • Full file submitted to the AD bank
    • Bank scrutiny, discrepancy queries answered by Flyport
    • Surplus earnings figure confirmed with the bank
    • Remittance instruction issued
    Week 4
    • Remittance executed to Vietnam Airlines head office
    • Post facto approval file lodged with Bangladesh Bank
    • CAAB traffic, cargo and mail statistics filed
    • Retained document custody updated for inspection readiness
    Monthly
    Bangladesh Bank reporting
    Monthly
    Post facto approval filing
    Monthly
    CAAB statistics return
    Fortnightly
    BSP and CASS settlement
    Presenter noteIf the airline's own finance team wants a single ask from this deck, it is this: get the disbursement challans to week one. Everything downstream depends on it.

    11  .  Risk register

    Six places a Bangladesh launch reliably loses time, and what removes each one.

    Risk 01  .  High

    Waiver clauses discovered late

    The BIDA permission arrives, the account opens, and only at the first remittance does anyone read the outward remittance restrictions.

    Mitigation Waivers are applied for with the permission, not after it.

    Risk 02  .  High

    Form FF not collected at booking

    Cargo freight collected in taka without the supporting Form FF cannot be remitted, and the shipper has no incentive to help months later.

    Mitigation Form FF is a condition of documentation release at the cargo desk.

    Risk 03  .  Medium

    Ledger mapped monthly, settlement fortnightly

    Annexure A expects fortnightly BSP and CASS splits. A monthly management ledger will not reconcile to it and the file gets referred back.

    Mitigation Reporting is built on the settlement calendar from month one.

    Risk 04  .  Medium

    Tax exemption certificate lapses

    The certificate expires quietly and the bank applies full withholding to a treaty exempt remittance. Recovery is slow.

    Mitigation Expiry sits on the same monthly review as the remittance file.

    Risk 05  .  Medium

    Insufficient funds in the designated account

    Remittance may only be made out of funds available in the account, without borrowing. A timing mismatch simply stops the transfer.

    Mitigation Disbursement timing is planned against the settlement calendar.

    Risk 06  .  Watch

    Regulatory drift

    The Foreign Exchange Operation Department issues circulars continuously. A process built on a superseded instruction fails quietly.

    Mitigation The circular index is re-checked before each annual review.

    Presenter noteRisks one and two are the ones that actually cost carriers money in this market. If time is short, cover those two and hand over the page.
